gaps.note: the maker says the door "opens up or down" and can be removed; the format has no hinge, so the door is drawn as one fitted plate that lifts off, and the swing is not stated.
gaps.wanted: a format that can say a hinged cover, and a close picture of the door's edge

gaps.note: the installation instructions give "two to four" equipment mounting screws for the range of heights and "one screw for every mounting hole", and no document gives the holes' positions or count for this height.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the back plate
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

attrs.note: datasheet - materials, finishes and the indoor-only statement are the data sheet's specifications table (page 2, "Steel, aluminum, and plastic T-shaped cable guides"; "Black or Glacier White powder coat paint"; "For indoor use only, in environmentally controlled areas; may not be used outdoors, in harsh environments or in air-handling spaces"). BABA compliance is the product page's for the 2U sibling. The part is not RoHS-stated by any document held.

bottom.note: estimated - the pictures show the same fingers along the bottom as along the top; the bottom is the top again.

capacity.note: datasheet - the maker's CPI Cable Fill Table (updated 2024; the data sheet's "Cable Fill" row points to chatsworth.com/cablefill, which links it) lists 35441-X01, Evolution Horizontal Cable Manager, 1U: interior width 0.9 in, interior depth 6.5 in, usable area 5.5 sq in; recommended fill 44 Cat 5e (0.200 in OD), 28 Cat 6 (0.250 in) and 19 Cat 6a (0.300 in); maximum fill 88, 56 and 39. The table's notes give recommended as 25% of the usable area and maximum as 50%. The figure stated is the maximum for Cat 6, 56, as the FS managers state their theoretical maximum for Cat6; the recommended 28 is in the basis.

chassis.note: datasheet - 1U x 19" EIA x 8.2" (208 mm) for 35441-X01 in the data sheet's ordering table, chassis style solid, with the note "1U horizontal managers available with solid chassis only". The width is the 482.6 of 19 in EIA, ears included, as a rack-face part is its ears and what hangs off them. The height is the 44.45 of one unit at the EIA-310 1.75 in. The depth is the maker's overall projection from the rail face, door and fingers included, and not a body depth.

color.note: estimated - black, or Glacier White (the colour letter X in the part number: 7 black, E Glacier White). The black is the maker's renders'; the Glacier White shade is not given by any document and is drawn a light grey.

door.note: datasheet - "Contoured, snap-on front door opens up or down" (data sheet and product page), "The cover will open up or down and can be removed when cabling" (installation instructions). The door is its own part, fitted as shipped, so a drawing can take it off and show the fingers; the format has no hinge, so that it swings up or down is a gap.

ears.note: estimated - the 16.3 of ear each end is half of the 32.6 between the 450.0 the manager's body is taken to fill (the EIA-310 clear opening between the rails, 17.72 in, to 450) and the 482.6 overall. No document gives the ear width. The ears are the ends of the back plate and are drawn with it, as the rack-face FS parts draw theirs; their mounting holes are not drawn, because the installation instructions give only "two to four" screws for the whole range of heights and no hole position.

fingers.note: estimated - T-SHAPED FINGERS, TOP AND BOTTOM, ON THE FRONT ONLY. The data sheet and installation instructions show the plastic T-shaped cable guides along the top edge and the bottom edge of the manager, standing from the back plate to the door (step 1: "the cover snaps onto the ends of the plastic, T-shaped cable guides (fingers)"). Nothing is on the back plate's far side. Ten fingers a row (nine slots counted across the width in the 2U to 4U pictures), 45.0 pitch, a 24.0 slot and a head that leaves an 8.0 neck. The finger plate is 11.4 thick, from the maker's interior width of 2.6 in for the 2U part; for the 1U part the interior width is 0.9 in (22.9 mm), which the 11.4 plates leave to within 1.3 mm. The pitch, slot and head are read off the pictures against the 450.0 between the ears and carry no tolerance.

front.note: estimated - the door, fitted. With it off, the two rows of finger heads. The `duct` guide is the 21.65 between the finger plates (44.45 less 2 x 11.4), over the 450.0 between the ears; the cable fill table's interior width for this part is 0.9 in (22.9 mm).

guides.note: estimated - the duct on the front view is the channel between the finger plates, run across the rack; finger pitch 45.0 and slot 24.0 as `fingers`.

left.note: estimated - the side: the back plate, the two finger plates 11.4 high with the cable space between them, and the door's face and returns at the front. No picture of the maker's is a side elevation; it is built from the front and plan figures.

method.note: FIGURES FROM A DATA SHEET TABLE AND FROM PICTURES. The Evolution Cable Management System data sheet (page 3, Evolution Horizontal Cable Managers table) states each part's height in rack units, 19" EIA, 8.2" (208 mm) deep, chassis style and shipping weight, and its pictures show the four chassis styles; the installation instructions (IIS-735441, Rev.3) draw the door off and on. NO DOCUMENT HOLDS A DIMENSIONED DRAWING: every figure below that is not the data sheet's table is read off a render or a line drawing and is `estimated`, with how. The maker's cable fill table (CPI Cable Fill Table, 2024) gives the interior width and depth of the manager, which fixes the finger plate and the cable space. The pictures are of 2U to 4U parts; none shows the 1U part, which is drawn as the same manager made shorter.

mount.note: drawing - the installation instructions' steps 2 and 3: the chassis is aligned to the desired rack unit and the mounting holes at its back line up with the rack's holes, one screw for every hole, "two to four" in all depending on the height. So the part bolts to the rail face at a rack unit and stands out from it, which is what `rack-face` says. The FS horizontal ducts are `rack` parts that state their units, so whether this line is `rack-face` or `rack` is a choice the pull request asks the owner to accept.

rear.note: datasheet - THE SOLID BACK PLATE. The ordering table lists 35441-X01 as solid, and the data sheet's "Solid back shown" picture, of a taller part, shows an unbroken plate. The plate's ears are the ends of the plate; their mounting holes are not drawn.

shell.note: estimated - A SHEET BODY, NOT A BOX: the back plate as a well 206 deep, the two rows of fingers standing in it, the door in it across the finger heads, which lifts off and opens the manager. The data sheet says "welded and riveted frame/door attaches to all CPI Rack Systems with supplied tool-less mounting hardware".

thickness.note: estimated - no document states a gauge. 1.5 is the steel of comparable rack-face parts in this library (the FS FHD-CMP5DR, 1.5 mm cold-rolled), since the data sheet says only "steel, aluminum, and plastic T-shaped cable guides".

top.note: estimated - the plan, rear at y=0: the back plate 2.0 thick, the finger plate to the door, nine slots 24.0 wide on a 45.0 pitch from 22 to 186 deep with rounded roots, narrowing to the 8.0 neck under the door's 16 mm return. Read off the 2U to 4U data sheet pictures; no view of the maker's is orthographic.

weight.note: datasheet - 3 lb (1.4 kg) in the data sheet's ordering table: its column is SHIPPING weight, so the carton is in it and the manager itself weighs less. No net weight is stated by any document held; the figure is stated as the weight so the part has one, and is an upper bound.
